currentContext.strengths: Integrated manufacturer able to process variable-composition coal tar and 'dirty'/impure feedstock economically into battery-acceptable, aluminium-grade and speciality materials - a capability few peers replicate|In-house logistics moat: owns and operates a fleet of 292 specialised heated tankers (built since 2001-02) delivering molten Coal Tar Pitch at 250C directly to customer plants, eliminating solidification/downtime risk and enabling just-in-time delivery|R&D-led product pioneering: first-to-market track record in India for various Coal Tar Pitch grades, Speciality Carbon Black grades and lithium-ion battery anode/cathode materials; developed a Zero-QI pitch grade outside Japan and a specialised defence-grade pitch for missile nose-cone thermal protection developed from scratch with no reverse-engineering reference|Deep in-house R&D capability - 180+ scientists including 28 PhDs, R&D spend of Rs129 crore in FY26|ESG as a commercial licence to operate: Board-level ESG governance, external assurance and quantified intensity reductions cited by customers as a factor in supplier selection; 8 zero-liquid-discharge manufacturing facilities and in-house clean power meeting 100% of electrical energy requirement|Three-decade-plus customer relationships built on reliability of supply ('For life')
currentContext.strategies: Deliberate transformation from 'a coal tar derivatives company' into 'a global advanced materials and application-driven solutions company'|Broadbasing the product portfolio through an integrated approach where end products become raw materials for other products|Strategic focus on shifting mix towards value-added products (Speciality Carbon Black, New Energy Materials) to fuel profitability growth rather than pursuing scale alone|Seeding the business with advanced, technology-intensive New Energy Materials products (lithium-ion battery anode and cathode active materials) to capitalise on the global energy transition|Growth via a complement of initiatives - acquisition, expansion, distribution, service and branding - to accelerate scale (e.g. Birla Tyres acquisition, Sicona Technologies investment, International Battery Company stake)|Expansion into liquid Coal Tar Pitch exports and international markets, including a dedicated high-temperature liquid pitch terminal at Haldia Port and first export shipment from Mangalore Port to the Middle East|Partnership-led access to external R&D/AI capability (International Battery Company stake) to accelerate the lab-to-commercialisation journey for New Energy Materials products|Board recommended/AGM notice proposes a final dividend of Rs 0.80 per equity share (80% of Rs 1 face value) for FY 2025-26, to be approved by shareholders at the 38th AGM on 11 June 2026.
currentContext.expansion: Himadri's capacity build-out has run in phases over four decades: coal tar distillation plants at Howrah, a new distillation plant and capacity expansions at Mahistikry (Hooghly), a manufacturing plant at Korba (Chhattisgarh), an SNF plant acquisition at Vapi (Gujarat), Carbon Black production with captive power at Hooghly, a brownfield power-plant expansion (12 MW to 20 MW, 2012), a major brownfield project raising India coal tar distillation capacity by 60% (2014), and a pitch-melting plant at Sambalpur (Odisha, commissioned 2016-17). More recently the Company commenced 60,000 TPA of Speciality Carbon Black production at Mahistikry and, in a brownfield expansion, added a further 70,000 TPA of speciality blacks with commercial production starting February 2026, taking total Speciality Carbon Black capacity to 1,30,000 TPA - stated to be the world's largest single-site facility for Speciality Carbon Black. On the New Energy Materials side, Himadri commissioned a commercial-scale lithium-ion battery anode active material facility and has a pilot-to-commercial LFP Cathode Active Material project underway (stated to be a first at commercial scale outside China). Export infrastructure has been expanded with a high-temperature liquid Coal Tar Pitch terminal at Haldia Port and a new liquid CTP terminal at New Mangalore (first shipment of 3,600 tonnes, December 2025), plus the first Middle East export shipment from Mangalore Port in November 2025. Forward integration into anthraquinone and carbazole is stated to be on track for commissioning in FY 2026-27.
currentContext.mdna: EBITDA growth attributed to stable volumes combined with higher margins, with continuing strategic focus on value-added products cited as the driver of profitability growth|Standalone revenue from operations declined ~4% YoY while EBITDA rose 16% YoY, indicating margin/mix improvement offsetting a revenue contraction|Demand for Himadri's carbon materials is linked to downstream end-market growth across aluminium smelting, graphite electrodes/battery cells, construction additives, agrochemicals, printing inks, tyres, paints, plastics, technical rubber goods and lithium-ion batteries - company frames its outlook as 'if the Indian or global economy grows, we grow'|Lithium-ion battery end-market cited as the fastest-growing demand driver, with the Indian market's energy demand from LiBs projected (per cited third-party research) to grow at a 39.3% CAGR from 2025 to 2030|Aluminium end-market demand (Coal Tar Pitch as smelting/electrode binder) linked to energy transition and infrastructure growth, with the Indian aluminium market projected (per cited third-party research) to grow at a 6.9% volume CAGR from 2025 to 2030

risks.risk: Strategic risk - cyclicality in downstream industries and pace of adoption in energy-transition segments
risks.note: Demand is tied to cyclical downstream industries (aluminium, steel/graphite) and to how fast New Energy Materials end-markets adopt; company cites Coal Tar Pitch demand from aluminium smelting as relatively inelastic (smelters cannot shut down without catastrophic restart costs) and relies on portfolio diversification across end-use industries as mitigation.

risks.risk: Feedstock and input volatility risk - price and availability fluctuations in raw materials
risks.note: Company depends on coal-tar-linked feedstock whose availability is tied to external coke-oven/steel production trends (including China); mitigated via pass-through pricing transparency with customers, backward integration, long-term sourcing relationships and converting internal by-products into value-added downstream products.

risks.risk: Technology and scale-up risk - commercialisation challenges in advanced materials and new chemistries
risks.note: New Energy Materials (anode/cathode active materials) and other advanced-materials initiatives carry execution risk in moving from pilot/semi-commercial to full commercial scale; company states it uses phased scale-up with defined performance milestones and has slowed/paused certain initiatives rather than force premature scale.

risks.risk: Operational concentration risk - large integrated manufacturing complexes create single-site exposure
risks.note: Concentration of production in large integrated manufacturing complexes exposes the Company to single-site disruption risk; mitigated by redundant utilities/logistics infrastructure, preventive maintenance and disaster-preparedness protocols.

risks.risk: Regulatory and sustainability risk - tightening environmental, safety and compliance norms
risks.note: Operating in a carbon-intensive chemicals value chain exposes the Company to tightening environmental/safety/compliance norms (including carbon-regulation and trade-compliance frameworks referenced elsewhere in the report); mitigation is early adoption of cleaner processes and investing in compliance ahead of regulation.

risks.risk: Financial and liquidity risk - capital intensity and working-capital volatility
risks.note: The business is capital intensive with working-capital volatility; company states growth is largely funded through internal accruals with conservative leverage and strong cash buffers as risk mitigation.

one-line thesis: Himadri is compounding earnings faster than revenue as its mix shifts to value-added and battery materials: consolidated revenue +28% and PAT +27% to Rs 228 cr (22% EBITDA margin), while it opened three new value ladders in one quarter — indigenous Carbon Nanotube (India-first), Super Speciality Carbon Black, and Anthraquinone/Carbazole (India's first commercial plant). The energy-materials build (200 MTPA anode commissioned Apr-2026; 2,000 MTPA LFP cathode by Q3FY27 scaling to 40,000 by FY28 and an ultimate 200,000 MTPA) is the long-dated option, all self-funded with no incremental debt, and the FY28 PAT target of Rs 1,100 cr was explicitly reaffirmed.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **PAT Rs 1,100 cr by FY28 reaffirmed** ("remains intact… I'll remain at INR1,100 Crores for next year"). No quarterly/annual revenue guidance given by policy.
- **Capex ~Rs 2,000 cr total** (Rs 1,125 cr LFP + Rs 368 cr CNT+SSCB announced this quarter + ~Rs 500 cr Birla Tyres): **~Rs 1,000 cr FY27 + ~Rs 1,000 cr FY28, fully self-funded, no incremental debt** (free cash flow covers).
- **CNT:** 200 MTPA, capex ~Rs 70 cr, commissioning **Q4FY27** (revenue small, <Rs 100 cr).
- **Super Speciality Carbon Black:** 6,000 MTPA (convert commodity capacity), capex Rs 170 cr, start **FY28**, revenue ~Rs 500 cr (3x asset turn), "significantly higher margins."
- **LFP cathode:** 2,000 MTPA **Q3FY27**; 40,000 MTPA operational **FY28** (Rs 1,125 cr capex → ~Rs 3,000 cr revenue); ultimate **200,000 MTPA in ~5 years** (Rs 4,800 cr announced) = 2-3% global LFP share.
- **Anthraquinone/Carbazole:** 5,300 MTPA total, full **FY28** (2,600 MTPA Q2FY27 + 2,700 MTPA Q2FY28), revenue Rs 250-300 cr; India's first commercial plant.
- **Coal-tar/carbon-black capacity utilization → 90%+** during FY27 (from ~80%).
- **Birla Tyres: EBITDA break-even + cash positive in FY27**; Rs 3,000 cr topline target in 4-5 years; PCR (passenger-car-radial) facility by FY28.
- **IBC:** 7 GW India cell facility (using Himadri materials) operational **Q4FY27**.
order book & pipeline: Not a classic order book. Battery-materials pipeline = customer sampling (Sample A→B→C→D; ~1.5-2 yr approval cycle). Anode Sample B now supplied to many Indian + global OEMs/manufacturers; LFP Sample A approved (incl. IBC, which formed a strategic partnership after testing HSCL's LFP). Strategy is "lab-first, plant-later" — 2,000 MTPA LFP first so approvals complete by the time 40,000 MTPA commissions. Coal tar pitch >65% domestic share; liquid CTP terminals at Haldia + Mangalore commissioned for exports.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Coal Tar Pitch (anchor):** world's largest single-location integrated carbon complex, 600,000 MTPA distillation; >65% domestic share; ~80% utilization → 90%+ during year; supplies "at the lowest price globally."
- **Speciality Carbon Black:** 250,000 MT total capacity (130,000 MT speciality), 70+ speciality grades. Moving up the ladder to **Super Speciality Carbon Black** (6,000 MTPA, FY28, ~300,000 MT global niche market).
- **Carbon Nanotube (NEW):** indigenous graphene-based tech; 200 MTPA (Q4FY27, ~Rs 70 cr); 100x steel strength, copper conductivity; global market ~30,000 MT; global play (small India market).
- **New energy materials:** 200 MTPA anode plant (Mahistikry, commissioned Apr-2026, capex Rs 120 cr, ~Rs 120-130 cr revenue potential, a validation/approvals facility); LFP cathode 2,000 MTPA (Q3FY27) → 40,000 (FY28) → 200,000 (5 yrs); also natural graphite + Si-C (via Sicona) — "hybrid material" optionality.
- **Anthraquinone/Carbazole (NEW):** 5,300 MTPA (2,600 Q2FY27 + 2,700 Q2FY28), India's first commercial plant, import substitution.
- **Birla Tyres:** commercial since 29-May-2025; Q1 sales Rs 127 cr; converting Truck/Bus-Bias → Off-the-Road (OTR) over 3 yrs; 49 distributors, 1,000+ dealers; 3 new agri SKUs (AGRIWIN/AGRIPLUS/AGRILEAP T40); 400+ SKUs in development; PCR by FY28. Currently on Dalmia Refractory balance sheet (revenue recognized in Himadri consol).
- **Strategic investees:** Sicona (Si-C anode; raised AUD 45M); IBC (~19%; prismatic cell tech ex-China, Seoul plant + 7 GW India facility by Q4FY27).
growth verticals / optionality: 1) **LFP cathode** — first non-China commercial-scale, 200,000 MTPA in 5 yrs (2-3% global share). 2) **Anode** — backward-integrated (own special engineered pitch), synthetic + natural + Si-C hybrid. 3) **CNT** — new-age advanced material, high-margin, global. 4) **Super Speciality Carbon Black** — multi-fold value-add over speciality. 5) **Anthraquinone/Carbazole** — import substitution, export optionality. 6) **Birla Tyres OTR + PCR/EV** — Rs 3,000 cr topline optionality.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Full backward integration from feedstock to material** — only anode player that is backward-integrated (own coal-tar-based special engineered pitch), giving cost efficiency, feedstock flexibility and resilience; "first company in the world to supply precursor from pitch to the who's-who of anode in China before China could make coal-tar-based precursors."
- **No China / no West-Asia dependence** — posted strong numbers through the West-Asia crisis; not exposed to Chinese dumping/pricing for any product; India production base + differentiated raw-material sourcing gives an LFP cost edge "compared to China."
- **World's largest single-location coal-tar complex** (600,000 MTPA, >65% domestic share) supplied "at the lowest price globally" — scale + integration anchor.
- **R&D depth** — Rs 125+ cr (2.6% of topline) FY26, 10-12 years on Li-ion; EcoVadis Platinum (top 1% globally) increasingly a commercial prerequisite in global value chains.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margins at record highs from mix-up-shift + in-house conversion of intermediates (not inventory gains); RM cost increases passed through. Consol EBITDA margin 22% (standalone 24%). Other expenses ex-forex fell to ~Rs 148 cr (from ~Rs 172 cr Q4) on lower outbound freight + cost optimization. Forex hedging loss recurred (last such quarter per management). New capex products (CNT/SSCB/anthraquinone) all carry "significantly higher" margins with no direct comparison to current products (management declined to disclose exact margins).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Total ~Rs 2,000 cr announced: Rs 1,125 cr LFP + Rs 368 cr (CNT + SSCB, announced this quarter) + ~Rs 500 cr Birla Tyres → ~Rs 1,000 cr FY27 + ~Rs 1,000 cr FY28. No coal-tar-pitch capex (already 6 lakh tons). Commissioning ladder to watch: anthraquinone 2,600 MTPA Q2FY27; LFP 2,000 MTPA Q3FY27; CNT 200 MTPA Q4FY27; IBC 7 GW India Q4FY27; SSCB + LFP 40,000 + anthraquinone balance + PCR all FY28. Ultimate 200,000 MTPA LFP (Rs 4,800 cr) over 5 yrs.
capital allocation: Disciplined, self-funded — capex "entirely self-funded", free cash flow covers, **no incremental debt**; deliberately calibrated brownfield (asset productivity) vs greenfield (new capability). Strategic (not financial) investments in IBC (~19%, no plan to raise) and Sicona for validation/commercial display of Himadri materials in cells — explicitly **not** entering cell manufacturing. Funds parked in FD/MF for carry. Zero-liquid-discharge across plants.
risks & watch-items: 1) **Forex volatility** — hedging losses two quarters running (says done from next quarter). 2) **LFP economics vs China** — analyst skepticism on gross spread (lithium-carbonate sourcing undisclosed); management insists confidential cost edge. 3) **Battery-material approval cycle** — 1.5-2 yrs (Sample A-D); commercialization timeline undisclosed. 4) **Birla Tyres execution** — not yet EBITDA positive; TBB→OTR conversion + PCR over 3 yrs. 5) **Mining** — idle awaiting environmental clearance (3-6 months, no visibility). 6) **New-product margins undisclosed** — execution/realization unproven.
management quality / tone: Anurag Choudhary confident, vision-led and detailed on strategy/market-sizing (CNT, LFP, anode chemistries), but deliberately opaque on competitive specifics — declined LFP cost/sourcing, new-product margins, and commercialization timelines ("because of competitive nature… confidential"). Reaffirmed Rs 1,100 cr FY28 PAT firmly and self-funding "no incremental debt." Emphasizes "compounding philosophy," lab-first/plant-later discipline, and no China/West-Asia dependence. Refuses quarterly/annual guidance by policy. Tone: ambitious but execution-and-discipline framed.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The 200 MTPA anode plant is a validation asset, not a revenue line** — commissioned to get on the "front foot" for approvals (Sample A-D); real anode revenue waits on a bigger, yet-unannounced capex — so near-term battery-materials P&L impact is negligible despite the headlines.
- **IBC is a commercialization showcase, not a financial stake** — the ~19% investment exists so Himadri materials are "commercially used in cells" (Prabal 2000/3000) and to seed a 7 GW India cell plant (Q4FY27) that consumes Himadri LFP/anode/Si-C — a demand pull, not portfolio return.
- **Earnings-over-revenue is explicit strategy** — intermediates consumed in-house and converted to value-added products, so volume can fall while revenue/margin rise; "next quarter you'll see top line growth from both volume and value."
- **Three new value ladders in one quarter (CNT/SSCB/anthraquinone) are the near-term margin story**, layered ahead of the long-dated LFP option — all self-funded, all "significantly higher" margin, all import-substitution/global-niche.

6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Full backward integration from feedstock to material** — only anode player that is backward-integrated (own coal-tar-based special engineered pitch), giving cost efficiency, feedstock flexibility and resilience; "first company in the world to supply precursor from pitch to the who's-who of anode in China before China could make coal-tar-based precursors."

non-obvious takeaways:
- **The 200 MTPA anode plant is a validation asset, not a revenue line** — commissioned to get on the "front foot" for approvals (Sample A-D); real anode revenue waits on a bigger, yet-unannounced capex — so near-term battery-materials P&L impact is negligible despite the headlines.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Himadri Speciality Chemical is an integrated manufacturer of speciality carbon products - Coal Tar Pitch, Carbon Black, Naphthalene, Refined Naphthalene, SNF and Speciality Oils - derived from coal tar distillation, serving steel, aluminium, graphite, tyre, automotive, paints, fibres, printing-ink and infrastructure customers. It has extended from its conventional carbon-chemicals base into a New Energy Materials business (lithium-ion battery anode active material, with a LFP cathode active material facility under development) as a strategic push into the energy-transition value chain.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- EBITDA growth attributed to stable volumes combined with higher margins, with continuing strategic focus on value-added products cited as the driver of profitability growth
- Standalone revenue from operations declined ~4% YoY while EBITDA rose 16% YoY, indicating margin/mix improvement offsetting a revenue contraction
- Demand for Himadri's carbon materials is linked to downstream end-market growth across aluminium smelting, graphite electrodes/battery cells, construction additives, agrochemicals, printing inks, tyres, paints, plastics, technical rubber goods and lithium-ion batteries - company frames its outlook as 'if the Indian or global economy grows, we grow'

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Himadri's capacity build-out has run in phases over four decades: coal tar distillation plants at Howrah, a new distillation plant and capacity expansions at Mahistikry (Hooghly), a manufacturing plant at Korba (Chhattisgarh), an SNF plant acquisition at Vapi (Gujarat), Carbon Black production with captive power at Hooghly, a brownfield power-plant expansion (12 MW to 20 MW, 2012), a major brownfield project raising India coal tar distillation capacity by 60% (2014), and a pitch-melting plant at Sambalpur (Odisha, commissioned 2016-17). More recently the Company commenced 60,000 TPA of Speciality Carbon Black production at Mahistikry and, in a brownfield expansion, added a further 70,000 TPA of speciality blacks with commercial production starting February 2026, taking total Speciality Carbon Black capacity to 1,30,000 TPA - stated to be the world's largest single-site facility for Speciality Carbon Black. On the New Energy Materials side, Himadri commissioned a commercial-scale lithium-ion battery anode active material facility and has a pilot-to-commercial LFP Cathode Active Material project underway (stated to be a first at commercial scale outside China). Export infrastructure has been expanded with a high-temperature liquid Coal Tar Pitch terminal at Haldia Port and a new liquid CTP terminal at New Mangalore (first shipment of 3,600 tonnes, December 2025), plus the first Middle East export shipment from Mangalore Port in November 2025. Forward integration into anthraquinone and carbazole is stated to be on track for commissioning in FY 2026-27.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated manufacturer able to process variable-composition coal tar and 'dirty'/impure feedstock economically into battery-acceptable, aluminium-grade and speciality materials - a capability few peers replicate
- In-house logistics moat: owns and operates a fleet of 292 specialised heated tankers (built since 2001-02) delivering molten Coal Tar Pitch at 250C directly to customer plants, eliminating solidification/downtime risk and enabling just-in-time delivery
- R&D-led product pioneering: first-to-market track record in India for various Coal Tar Pitch grades, Speciality Carbon Black grades and lithium-ion battery anode/cathode materials; developed a Zero-QI pitch grade outside Japan and a specialised defence-grade pitch for missile nose-cone thermal protection developed from scratch with no reverse-engineering reference
- Deep in-house R&D capability - 180+ scientists including 28 PhDs, R&D spend of Rs129 crore in FY26
- ESG as a commercial licence to operate: Board-level ESG governance, external assurance and quantified intensity reductions cited by customers as a factor in supplier selection; 8 zero-liquid-discharge manufacturing facilities and in-house clean power meeting 100% of electrical energy requirement
- Three-decade-plus customer relationships built on reliability of supply ('For life')

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) **Forex volatility** — hedging losses two quarters running (says done from next quarter). 2) **LFP economics vs China** — analyst skepticism on gross spread (lithium-carbonate sourcing undisclosed); management insists confidential cost edge. 3) **Battery-material approval cycle** — 1.5-2 yrs (Sample A-D); commercialization timeline undisclosed. 4) **Birla Tyres execution** — not yet EBITDA positive; TBB→OTR conversion + PCR over 3 yrs. 5) **Mining** — idle awaiting environmental clearance (3-6 months, no visibility). 6) **New-product margins undisclosed** — execution/realization unproven.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The 200 MTPA anode plant is a validation asset, not a revenue line** — commissioned to get on the "front foot" for approvals (Sample A-D); real anode revenue waits on a bigger, yet-unannounced capex — so near-term battery-materials P&L impact is negligible despite the headlines.
- **IBC is a commercialization showcase, not a financial stake** — the ~19% investment exists so Himadri materials are "commercially used in cells" (Prabal 2000/3000) and to seed a 7 GW India cell plant (Q4FY27) that consumes Himadri LFP/anode/Si-C — a demand pull, not portfolio return.
- **Earnings-over-revenue is explicit strategy** — intermediates consumed in-house and converted to value-added products, so volume can fall while revenue/margin rise; "next quarter you'll see top line growth from both volume and value."
- **Three new value ladders in one quarter (CNT/SSCB/anthraquinone) are the near-term margin story**, layered ahead of the long-dated LFP option — all self-funded, all "significantly higher" margin, all import-substitution/global-niche.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deliberate transformation from 'a coal tar derivatives company' into 'a global advanced materials and application-driven solutions company'
- Broadbasing the product portfolio through an integrated approach where end products become raw materials for other products
- Strategic focus on shifting mix towards value-added products (Speciality Carbon Black, New Energy Materials) to fuel profitability growth rather than pursuing scale alone
- Seeding the business with advanced, technology-intensive New Energy Materials products (lithium-ion battery anode and cathode active materials) to capitalise on the …

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Consol revenue Rs 1,432 cr (+28%), EBITDA Rs 313 cr (+33%, 22%), PAT Rs 228 cr (+27%, 16%); standalone Rs 1,274 cr / Rs 301 cr / Rs 223 cr. Three NEW businesses announced: CNT (200 MTPA, Rs 70 cr, Q4FY27), Super Speciality Carbon Black (6,000 MTPA, Rs 170 cr, FY28, ~Rs 500 cr rev), Anthraquinone/Carbazole (5,300 MTPA, FY28, Rs 250-300 cr rev). Anode 200 MTPA commissioned Apr-2026 (validation, Rs 120 cr); LFP 2,000 MTPA Q3FY27 → 40,000 FY28 (Rs 1,125 cr → Rs 3,000 cr rev) → 200,000 in 5 yrs (Rs 4,800 cr, 2-3% global). Birla Tyres Rs 127 cr sales (not yet EBITDA+; break-even + cash-positive targeted FY27; Rs 3,000 cr in 4-5 yrs). IBC ~19%, 7 GW India cell plant Q4FY27. Capex ~Rs 2,000 cr (Rs 1,000 FY27 + Rs 1,000 FY28), self-funded no debt. Forex loss (last quarter of impact). Utilization 80% → 90%+. **PAT Rs 1,100 cr FY28 reaffirmed.**
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (1) anthraquinone 2,600 MTPA commissioning (Q2FY27); (2) forex loss actually gone; (3) volume-led + value-led topline growth return; (4) Birla Tyres toward EBITDA break-even; (5) mining env-clearance / restart; (6) anode Sample B → C progress; (7) utilization toward 90%+; (8) capex pace vs ~Rs 1,000 cr FY27._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Birla Tyres] Himadri, with resolution applicant DBRL, acquired Birla Tyres in Oct 2023; the plant has been recommissioned and the brand is nearing double-digit market share in select geographies with 49 distributors (40 domestic, 9 global), 1,000+ dealers and 145+ SKUs.
- [IBC] The 19.44% stake in Silicon Valley-headquartered International Battery Company comes with a nominee director seat; IBC turned revenue-generating in FY24-25, runs a 50 MWh cell plant since 2023 and has India gigafactory commercial operations on track for Q4FY27 via an asset-light technology partnership model.
- [Sicona] Sicona's SiCx silicon-carbon anode platform claims 20%+ higher energy density and 40%+ faster charging as a drop-in solution, has secured up to AUD 45 million of ARENA funding, and is engaged with 39 global OEMs/cell makers under NDA with 14 active qualification programmes.
- [Invati] The 40% stake in Invati Creations (two Himadri nominee directors) covers nanotech-enabled electrode formulation platforms and patented novel molecules, with R&D extending into energy storage and life sciences.
- [Ambition] Management states it expects to compress the growth achieved across three decades into just the next few years, with significant sustainable profitability growth targeted over the next two years.
